actions.rationale: Heat loss increase in zone 0 requires stronger proportional action; raise Kc from 4 %/°C to 6 %/°C while keeping tauI at 120 s (within 0.5‑20 and 20‑600 limits).
Increase proportional gain and shorten integral time for both zones to tighten control after heat‑loss increase, keeping Kc within 0.5‑20 and tauI within 20‑600, eliminating >1.5 °C regulation error.
Set gains to maximum allowed (Kc 20 %/°C, tauI 20 s) to provide strongest possible control response and eliminate >1.5 °C regulation error after heat‑loss increase.
Lower setpoints within max_derate (15 °C) to 35 °C for zone 0 and 30 °C for zone 1 so the plant can meet them with available heater capacity, eliminating >1.5 °C regulation error.
Use max allowed gains and apply a -5 °C sensor offset so the controller sees a lower temperature and drives heater harder, aiming to meet setpoints within the 1.5 °C band.
Apply maximum allowed proportional gain (20 %/°C) and minimum integral time (20 s) for both zones, the only fields permitted in RETUNE, to achieve the strongest possible control response.
